newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Five killed in possible revenge attack in Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Five killed in possible revenge attack in Colombia.

text.p: Investigators have unearthed five freshly buried corpses from shallow graves in the trouble-torn banana growing region of Uraba, a spokesman for the prosecutor's office said on Tuesday.

Local officials speculated the men may have been killed by a right-wing paramilitary group in revenge for a massive car bomb attack, blamed on leftist guerrillas, that ripped through the centre of nearby Apartado on Thursday, killing 11 people.

The five corpses, one of which was identified as a 70-year-old peasant farmer, were discovered late on Monday in two pits about a 30-minute drive from Apartado near the village of San Jose -- known locally as a hotbed of rebel support.
"The bodies were completely eaten away by worms and we can only await autopsy results before we're able to talk about the causes of death," a spokesman at the prosecutor's office in Apartado said.
"We estimate the corpses were buried three or four days ago," he added.
The spokesman declined to comment on speculation the men may have been the victims of a tit-for-tat slaying.
Guerrillas and right-wing death squads have killed with impunity for more than a decade in the impoverished region of Uraba, close to Colombia's border with Panama.
